newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda plans to open stock market in April.
newsitem.headline: Uganda plans to open stock market in April.

text.p: Uganda will open its stock exchange within a month, although it has still to find a trading floor, Capital Markets Authority Chairman Leo Kibirango said.

"The latest period possible will be about a month from now for the stock exchange to start," he told reporters on Tuesday at the official announcement of licenses for Uganda's first dealer/brokers and investment advisers.

The exchange was originally scheduled to open in September last year on a floor of the East African Development Bank in the heart of Kampala. But delays to renovation of the building have repeatedly postponed the opening.
"We understand now that even by end of March it may not be ready," Kibirango said. However, the Capital Markets Authority would help the exchange find a trading floor within the next month.

The authority expects about five companies to be listed on the exchange in its first year of operation, all of them newly-privatised, including Uganda Grain Milling Co Ltd, Uganda Consolidated Properties Ltd and National Insurance Corp.

It announced licences for seven firms to act as dealer/brokers or investment advisers, with some taking on both roles. They are: African Alliance Uganda Ltd, a subsidiary of Capital Alliance Holding Co of South Africa, PMC (MBEA) Investment (Private) Ltd, a subsidiary of PMC & Co Inc of the United States, Stanbic International, a wholly-owned unit of SIBC Africa Holding Ltd, Dyer and Blair (U) Ltd, Greenland Finance, Crane Financial Services and Uganda Commercial Bank.
Kibirango said a memorandum of understanding signed last week between Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya would open the way to cross-border listings and the establishment of a regional stock exchange.

"The successful integration of the markets at the regional level will offer a wide enough variation of securities and adequate depth in terms of participants to make it possible to attract foreign investors into the markets," he said.
